newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai '96 financial sector turnover up 26.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai '96 financial sector turnover up 26.6 pct.

text.p: The volume of business done by banking and insurance companies in Shanghai, China's financial hub, grew 26.6 percent in 1996 to 32.4 billion yuan ($3.9 billion), the official Xinhua news agency said.
Securities trading in the city quadrupled in 1996 to more than 2.76 trillion yuan, it said, quoting recent figures.
Xinhua gave no details on the origin of the figures.
Turnover of treasury bonds in Shanghai grew nine-fold year-on-year to 1.74 trillion yuan in 1996, it said, while the volume of shares traded in the city almost doubled to 911 billion yuan.
The value of currencies traded in Shanghai in 1996 was more than $62.8 billion, Xinhua said. Last year's interbank transactions were worth 587.1 billion yuan.
Premiums paid to Chinese insurance companies based in Shanghai grew 30 percent in 1996 over the 1995 figure to 5.24 billion yuan, Xinhua said.

It said official data showed there were 2,540 domestic financial institutions in Shanghai by the end of 1996, and 193 overseas financial institutions and representative offices, more than in any other Chinese city.
